en: be concluded; be signed (of a contract)

examples.en: A contract was concluded between the two companies.
Once the agreement is signed, trade gets easier.
I'll send you the contract that was signed yesterday.

examples.ko: 조약이 체결되기 전에 회의를 세 번 했어요.
examples.en: They held three meetings before the treaty was concluded.
The contract will be signed next week.

examples.ko: 합의는 했지만 아직 계약이 체결되지 않았어요.
examples.en: We agreed, but the contract hasn't been signed yet.

explain: 계약·협정·조약처럼 문서로 남기는 약속에 써요. 사람이 주어가 아니라 계약이 주어라서 '계약이 체결되다'로 말하고, 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '계약을 체결하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '계약하다', '사인하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used for formal commitments put on paper: contracts, agreements, treaties. The contract is the subject ('계약이 체결되다'); when you name the people acting, use '계약을 체결하다'. In everyday talk Koreans usually say '계약하다' or '사인하다'.

en: own and keep; hold in a collection

examples.ko: 저는 오래된 우표를 많이 소장하고 있어요.
examples.en: I own a lot of old stamps in my collection.
This museum holds rare paintings.
I inherited the books my father had kept.

examples.ko: 친구는 만화책 전집을 소장하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My friend wants to own the complete comic book set.
The library kept that letter in its collection.
It's a record worth keeping in a collection.

explain: 그냥 '갖고 있다'가 아니라 값지거나 의미 있는 물건을 모아서 오래 간직한다는 느낌이 있어요. 박물관·도서관·수집가에게 잘 어울려요. 영상이나 전자책을 사서 평생 보관하는 것도 요즘은 '소장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Not just 'have': it implies keeping something valuable or meaningful for a long time, so it fits museums, libraries and collectors. These days buying a video or e-book to keep permanently is also called '소장'.

examples.en: It's a place where new value is created.
How was this work of art created?
The world wasn't created overnight.
When ideas come together, a new culture is created.

examples.ko: 그 이야기는 한 작가의 상상으로 창조된 세계예요.
examples.en: That story is a world created from one writer's imagination.
Many good jobs will be created.

explain: '만들어지다'보다 무겁고, 없던 것이 처음 생겨난다는 느낌이 강해요. 종교의 천지창조나 예술·문화·가치처럼 큰 것에 어울려요. 물건이 만들어질 때는 '만들어지다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Heavier than '만들어지다' and stresses that something brand new comes into being. It suits big things: creation in religion, art, culture, value. For ordinary objects, '만들어지다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The date was agreed on at the meeting.
Once the price is agreed, we sign right away.
I'll put what was agreed in writing.
Nothing has been agreed yet.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에 휴전이 합의될 것 같아요.
examples.en: A ceasefire seems likely to be agreed between the two countries.
I'm glad it was settled in a way everyone is happy with.

explain: '합의하다'는 사람이 주어이고, '합의되다'는 의견 차이가 정리된 결과를 말해요. 그래서 '날짜가 합의되다', '조건이 합의되다'처럼 주어가 안건이에요. 친구끼리는 보통 '정하다', '맞추다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '합의하다' has people as the subject; '합의되다' describes the result after differences are settled, so the subject is the item: 'the date was agreed'. Among friends, people usually say '정하다' or '맞추다' instead.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 아직 사용이 허가되지 않았어요.
examples.en: This building hasn't been approved for use yet.
It was approved a week after I applied.
Only people with permission can enter.
I'll let you know if filming is permitted.
I don't know whether an event will be allowed in the park.

examples.ko: 영업이 허가돼서 가게를 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: The business was licensed, so I can open the shop.

explain: 관청이나 책임자가 공식적으로 '해도 된다'고 정해 줄 때 써요. 허용되다는 규칙상 가능하다는 느낌이고, 허가되다는 신청하고 승인받는 절차가 떠올라요. 가족이나 친구에게 허락받는 건 '허락'이에요.
explain_en: Used when an authority officially says 'you may'. '허용되다' is closer to 'allowed by the rules', while '허가되다' suggests applying and getting approval. Getting a yes from family or friends is '허락', not '허가'.

examples.en: I got scammed in a secondhand deal.
My grandmother almost got scammed over the phone.
I want to get back the money I was scammed out of.
I heard that my friend got swindled.
Be careful not to get scammed at online shops.

examples.ko: 사기당하고 나서 아무도 못 믿게 됐어요.
examples.en: After being swindled, I couldn't trust anyone.

explain: 속인 사람은 '사기를 치다'라고 하고, 당한 사람은 '사기당하다'라고 해요. 가볍게 '속았다'고도 하는데, 돈을 잃는 큰 일이면 '사기당했다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: The scammer 'does' it ('사기를 치다'); the victim says '사기당하다'. People also say '속았다' casually, but when real money is lost, '사기당했다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The camera is fixed to the wall.
The injured leg was held in place with a bandage.
Once an idea is fixed in your mind, it's hard to change.

examples.ko: 월급이 고정되어 있어서 계획을 세우기 쉬워요.
examples.en: My salary is fixed, so it's easy to plan.
The screen is locked in place, so the text doesn't move.
The desk isn't fixed to the floor, so it wobbles.

explain: 나사·붕대처럼 흔들리지 않게 붙어 있을 때도, 생각·수입·역할처럼 안 바뀔 때도 써요. 붙이는 사람은 'A를 B에 고정하다', 붙어 있는 쪽은 '고정되다'예요. '고정관념', '고정 수입'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Used both when something is held firmly in place, like a screw or a bandage, and when something does not change, like an idea, an income or a role. The person who fixes it says 'A를 B에 고정하다'; the thing that stays put is '고정되다'. It also appears in front of other words, as in '고정관념' (fixed idea) and '고정 수입' (fixed income).

examples.en: The dove is a symbol of peace.
The Korean flag symbolizes the spirit of our country.
Red is a color that is seen as a symbol of passion.

examples.ko: 이 탑은 우리 도시의 역사로 상징돼서 관광객이 많아요.
examples.en: This tower is seen as a symbol of the city's history, so it has many tourists.
The heart came to be a symbol of love.
Think about what it will be symbolized by.

explain: 'A는 B로 상징된다'처럼 조사 '로'와 같이 써요. 상징하는 대상이 주어이고, 책이나 뉴스, 발표에서 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 'A 하면 B가 떠올라요'처럼 풀어서 많이 해요.
explain_en: Used in the pattern 'A는 B로 상징된다' with the particle '로'. The thing that stands for something is the subject. It shows up in books, news and presentations; in speech people often say 'A 하면 B가 떠올라요'.

en: select; choose through a test or screening

examples.ko: 회사에서 신입 사원을 열 명 선발해요.
examples.en: The company selects ten new employees.
The coach selected the players for the national team.
They will choose scholarship students by test score.

examples.ko: 선발된 학생들은 여름에 해외 연수를 가요.
examples.en: The selected students go abroad for training in summer.

examples.ko: 공정하게 선발하려고 면접을 두 번 봐요.
examples.en: To choose fairly, they hold two interviews.
The selection criteria are too hard.

explain: 시험·면접·경기 결과처럼 기준을 두고 여러 사람 중에서 뽑을 때 써요. '뽑다'는 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '선발하다'는 공식적인 자리의 말이에요. 반대로 뽑히는 쪽은 '선발되다', 떨어지면 '탈락하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when you pick people from a larger group by a standard such as a test, interview or match results. '뽑다' is the everyday word; '선발하다' is more official. The person chosen is '선발되다', and one who fails is '탈락하다'.

examples.en: Bus fares will be reduced from next month.
When interest rates are cut, loan interest goes down.
I saw an ad saying the price had been cut.

examples.ko: 인하된 가격에 물건을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy the item at the reduced price.
I wonder whether taxes will be cut.
I was disappointed that electricity rates weren't cut.

explain: 가격·요금·금리·세금처럼 숫자가 내려갈 때만 써요. 반대말은 '인상되다'인데, 발음이 비슷해서 헷갈리니까 '인하=아래, 인상=위'로 기억하세요. 가게에서는 보통 '싸졌다', '할인'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: Only for numbers that go down: prices, fees, interest rates, taxes. The opposite is '인상되다', and the two sound alike, so remember 인하 = down, 인상 = up. In shops people just say '싸졌다' or '할인'.

en: communicate; pass thoughts back and forth

examples.en: I try to communicate with my team often.

examples.ko: 말이 안 통해도 웃음으로 소통할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even without a shared language, we can connect through smiles.
Our manager communicates well with the staff.
I joined a group that communicates online.
I felt stuck because I couldn't connect with my parents.
After we talked it through, the misunderstanding cleared up.

explain: 그냥 말을 주고받는 것이 아니라, 마음과 생각이 서로 잘 통한다는 느낌이 있어요. 회사·가족·SNS 이야기에서 '소통이 안 돼요', '소통을 잘해요'처럼 자주 나와요. 단순히 정보를 전하는 건 '연락하다', '전달하다'가 맞아요.
explain_en: More than just exchanging words: it implies thoughts and feelings getting through to each other. Common in talk about work, family and social media, e.g. '소통이 안 돼요'. For simply passing on information, '연락하다' or '전달하다' fits better.

examples.en: Exercise reduces stress.
The company is trying to reduce costs.

examples.ko: 이 약은 통증을 감소시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can reduce pain.
I'm looking for ways to cut down on trash.
The new system greatly reduced accidents.
After reducing the noise, it became much quieter.

explain: '줄이다'와 같지만, 줄어드는 대상이 양·수치·비율처럼 측정되는 것일 때 글이나 보고서에서 많이 써요. 스스로 줄어들면 '감소하다'이고, 누군가가 줄게 만들면 '감소시키다'예요. 말할 때는 '줄이다'가 훨씬 흔해요.
explain_en: Same idea as '줄이다', but typical in reports and writing when the thing reduced is a measurable amount or rate. '감소하다' is when something decreases by itself; '감소시키다' is when someone makes it decrease. In speech, '줄이다' is far more common.

examples.en: The important parts are highlighted in red.
The importance of safety was stressed again.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 허리 라인이 강조되어 있어요.
examples.en: This outfit emphasizes the waistline.
We read emphasized words louder.
If that part is stressed too much, it feels heavy.
Prevention keeps being stressed in the news.

explain: '강조하다'가 말하는 사람이 힘주어 말하는 것이라면, '강조되다'는 글·화면·분위기에서 어떤 점이 눈에 띄는 것이에요. 색, 글자 크기, 반복으로 강조돼요. '강조하다'와 '부각되다'도 비슷하지만 부각되다는 저절로 두드러질 때 써요.
explain_en: If '강조하다' is a speaker putting weight on a point, '강조되다' is a point that stands out in text, a screen or the mood, through color, size or repetition. '부각되다' is similar but for things that stand out on their own.

examples.en: The two parts are firmly joined together.
When oxygen and hydrogen combine, they become water.
It's a design that combines tradition and modernity.

examples.ko: 여러 기술이 결합돼서 새 제품이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Several technologies were combined to produce a new product.
I bought a toy where blocks join together.
Different kinds of music sometimes get combined.

explain: 따로 있던 둘 이상이 하나로 붙을 때 써요. 부품, 화학 물질, 기술, 문화처럼 글과 설명에서 자주 나와요. '합쳐지다'는 더 일상적이고, '섞이다'는 형태가 사라지고 뒤섞일 때 써요.
explain_en: For two or more separate things becoming one: parts, chemicals, technologies, cultures. Common in writing and explanations. '합쳐지다' is the everyday version, and '섞이다' is for things that mix and lose their shape.

examples.en: Sunlight can damage your skin.
Overdoing exercise damages the knees.
I accidentally damaged the book cover.

examples.ko: 그 말이 그의 명예를 손상하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: That remark seems to damage his reputation.

examples.ko: 물건을 손상하지 않게 조심히 옮겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please move it carefully so you don't damage anything.
After damaging the machine, I paid for the repair.

explain: 물건·몸·평판이 상하거나 망가지게 할 때 써요. 물건이 저절로 상하면 '손상되다', 일상에서는 '망가지다', '다치다', '상하다'를 더 많이 말해요. '명예를 손상하다'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 써요.
explain_en: For making an object, body part or reputation damaged. When it happens by itself, use '손상되다'; in daily talk '망가지다', '다치다' and '상하다' are more common. It also works for invisible things: '명예를 손상하다'.

examples.en: They farm oysters in this area.
I met people who farm seaweed in the sea.
My father has farmed abalone since I was little.

examples.ko: 연어를 양식할 때는 물 온도가 중요해요.
examples.en: Water temperature matters when farming salmon.
Farmed fish is a little cheaper.

examples.ko: 좁은 곳에서 양식하다 보면 병이 쉽게 퍼져요.
examples.en: When you farm in a cramped place, disease spreads easily.

explain: 바다나 양어장에서 물고기·조개·김을 키워 거둘 때만 써요. 동물을 키울 때는 '키우다', 소나 돼지는 '사육하다'라고 해요. 바다에서 잡은 건 '자연산', 키운 건 '양식'이라고 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: Only for raising fish, shellfish or seaweed in the sea or fish farms. For animals in general use '키우다'; for cattle or pigs, '사육하다'. At the fish market, wild-caught is '자연산' and farmed is '양식'.

examples.en: This incident was highlighted heavily in the news.

examples.ko: 그동안 잘 알려지지 않은 이야기가 조명되고 있어요.
examples.en: A little-known story is now getting attention.
This documentary shines a light on teenage issues.

examples.ko: 새롭게 조명된 작가의 작품을 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I read the work of a writer who has recently been brought into focus.

examples.ko: 문제가 제대로 조명되면 해결도 빨라질 거예요.
examples.en: If the problem is properly brought to light, the solution will come faster.
His life is going to be portrayed in a film.

explain: 불빛이 비친다는 뜻에서 나와서, 사람들이 잘 몰랐던 일이 새롭게 주목받고 알려질 때 써요. 뉴스·방송·글에서 자주 보이고, 실제 전등이 켜진다는 뜻으로는 쓰지 않아요. 같은 뜻으로 '주목받다'를 쓰면 더 쉬운 말이에요.
explain_en: It comes from the image of light shining on something, and means a subject gets fresh attention. Seen in news, broadcasts and writing; you do not use it for a lamp actually turning on. '주목받다' is an easier near-equivalent.

en: be manipulated; be rigged; be faked

examples.en: That photo was faked.
There's a rumor that the vote results were rigged.
The video has been manipulated, so it's hard to believe.
If data is manipulated, the research becomes meaningless.

examples.ko: 뉴스가 조작될 수 있다는 걸 알아야 해요.
examples.en: You should know that news can be manipulated.
There's evidence that the scores weren't tampered with.

explain: 사실이 아닌데 일부러 꾸미거나 바꿔 놓았을 때 써요. 사진·영상·기록·점수에 많이 쓰고, 항상 나쁜 의미예요. 기계를 다루는 '조작하다'(버튼을 조작하다)와는 쓰임이 달라서 '조작되다'는 거짓으로 꾸민 쪽으로만 기억하세요.
explain_en: For something deliberately altered to look different from the truth: photos, videos, records, scores. Always negative. Don't confuse it with '조작하다' meaning 'operate' (a button or machine); the passive '조작되다' is used for faked things.

examples.en: Living things evolve to suit their environment.

examples.ko: 스마트폰은 몇 년 만에 크게 진화했어요.
examples.en: Smartphones have evolved a lot in just a few years.
I'm curious how AI will evolve.
It's hard to keep up with evolving technology.

examples.ko: 우리 가게도 시대에 맞게 진화하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our shop is also evolving with the times.
I cheer for the singer who came back in an evolved form.

explain: 생물학의 '진화'에서 나왔지만, 요즘은 기술·게임·가수의 실력이 한 단계 좋아졌을 때도 많이 써요. '발전하다'는 앞으로 나아가는 것, '진화하다'는 모습이나 방식 자체가 바뀌며 좋아지는 느낌이에요. 게임에서 캐릭터가 더 강한 모습으로 바뀔 때도 '진화'라고 해요.
explain_en: It comes from biological evolution, but nowadays also describes tech, games or a singer's skill stepping up a level. '발전하다' is moving forward; '진화하다' suggests the form or method itself changes for the better. In games, a character changing into a stronger form is also called '진화'.

examples.ko: 이 상을 받게 되어 정말 명예로워요.
examples.en: I'm truly honored to receive this award.
He retired with honor.
Defending the country is an honorable job.
I think we lost with honor.
The players can't forget the honorable moment.
It's an honorable position, but it carries heavy responsibility.

explain: 사람들에게 존경받을 만하거나 자랑스러운 일·자리·행동에 써요. 평범한 기쁨에는 어울리지 않아요. 상을 받거나 큰 역할을 맡을 때 '영광이에요'와 같이 격식 있게 말해요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '명예로워요'로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: For jobs, positions or deeds that earn respect and pride; it doesn't suit ordinary happiness. When receiving an award or a big role it works like '영광이에요' in formal speech. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '명예로워요'.

examples.ko: 이 사건은 지난달 일과 연관돼 있어요.
examples.en: This incident is connected to last month's event.
Health and sleep are deeply related.
I called in everyone involved and talked.
I don't want to be involved in that matter.
Check whether the two problems are connected.

examples.ko: 주제와 연관되지 않은 이야기는 빼 주세요.
examples.en: Please leave out stories unrelated to the topic.

explain: '관련되다'와 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 조사는 '~와/과 연관되다'를 써요. 사건이나 사람이 어떤 일에 얽혀 있을 때도 쓰고, 이 경우에는 조금 부정적인 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '관련이 있다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: Nearly interchangeable with '관련되다'. The pattern is '~와/과 연관되다'. When a person or event is tied up in some matter it can sound a bit negative. In daily talk '관련이 있다' is more common.

examples.en: If you link words with pictures, they're easy to memorize.
I associate that song with summer.
There's no evidence to link the two incidents.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 돈과 연관시키는 사람이 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like people who connect everything to money.
The teacher tied what we learned to everyday life.
Don't force a connection; just state the facts.

explain: 스스로 이어진 건 '연관되다', 누군가가 이은 건 '연관시키다'로 구분해요. '~을/를 ~와 연관시키다' 구조라서 목적어가 꼭 따라와요. 사람이 두 가지를 생각이나 행동으로 이어 놓을 때 써요.
explain_en: Things that connect by themselves are '연관되다'; when someone connects them, it is '연관시키다'. The structure is '~을/를 ~와 연관시키다', so it always takes an object. Use it when a person links two things in thought or action.

examples.en: The work changed suddenly, so my head is a mess.
Right after the accident, the scene was chaotic.
In chaotic times, act calmly.
The explanation is so complicated that I'm even more confused.

examples.ko: 마음이 혼란하면 일단 쉬는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When your mind is in turmoil, it's best to rest first.
I'm so confused that I don't know where to start.

explain: 머릿속이 정리되지 않을 때도, 사회나 장소가 질서 없이 뒤죽박죽일 때도 써요. '혼란스럽다'는 그런 느낌이 든다는 말이라 사람 마음에 더 자주 쓰이고, '혼란하다'는 상황·시기·현장에 어울려요. '복잡하다'는 얽혀 있다는 뜻이라 질서가 무너졌다는 느낌은 없어요.
explain_en: Covers both a muddled mind and a society or place without order. '혼란스럽다' is more about how you feel, while '혼란하다' fits situations, periods and scenes. '복잡하다' only means tangled, with no sense that order has collapsed.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 주로 젊은 층에서 소비돼요.
examples.en: This product is mainly consumed by young people.

examples.ko: 한 달에 전기가 얼마나 소비되는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check how much electricity is used in a month.
Too much time was used up.
I'll restock the food that was used.
We've entered an age where less rice is eaten.

examples.ko: 에너지가 이렇게 소비되면 곧 부족해질 거예요.
examples.en: If energy is used up like this, we'll run short soon.

explain: 돈·물건·에너지·시간이 쓰여서 줄어들 때 써요. 상품이 '팔린다'가 아니라 '쓰이고 사라진다'는 쪽에 가까워요. 사람이 주어이면 '소비하다', 물건이 주어이면 '소비되다'예요. 아껴 쓰는 건 '절약하다'예요.
explain_en: For money, goods, energy or time being used and running down; the focus is on being used up, not being sold. A person is the subject of '소비하다', while the thing is the subject of '소비되다'. Saving is '절약하다'.

examples.en: The two people's opinions came into agreement.
I trust people whose words and actions match.
It seems to match the culprit's fingerprint.
When we think alike, the work finishes fast.

examples.ko: 답이 서로 일치되지 않아서 다시 확인했어요.
examples.en: The answers didn't match, so I checked again.
Our tastes matched, so we quickly became close.

explain: 둘 이상이 어긋남 없이 딱 맞을 때 써요. 의견·시간·정보처럼 '맞다'로 말할 수 있는 것에 쓰고, 보통 '~와/과 일치하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 일치되다는 맞춰져 가는 과정이나 결과를 강조할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: For two or more things that match exactly: opinions, times, information. '~와/과 일치하다' is often more natural; '일치되다' fits when you stress the process or result of coming into line.

en: make something match; bring into line

examples.en: Please make the dates in the two documents match.
I try to make my words and actions match.
It's hard to line up everyone's schedules.
It looks much neater now that the colors match.
We played a game of matching photos with names.
We present after aligning our opinions.

explain: 사람이 일부러 두 가지를 서로 맞게 할 때 써요. 저절로 맞는 것은 '일치하다', 맞춰진 상태는 '일치되다', 맞추는 행동은 '일치시키다'예요. 일상에서는 '맞추다'가 더 쉽고 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when a person deliberately makes two things fit. '일치하다' matches by itself, '일치되다' is the matched state, and '일치시키다' is the act of matching. In daily speech '맞추다' is easier and more common.

examples.en: Photography is allowed here.
Pets aren't allowed in the dorm.
Dictionary use was allowed during the exam.

examples.ko: 허용된 시간 안에 문제를 풀어야 해요.
examples.en: You must solve the problems within the allowed time.

examples.ko: 조금 늦는 건 허용되지만 너무 늦으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Being a little late is tolerated, but not too late.

examples.ko: 이 정도 실수는 허용될 것 같아요.
examples.en: A mistake this small seems acceptable.

explain: 규칙이나 상황이 그렇게 하는 것을 막지 않을 때 써요. '허가되다'가 신청해서 받는 승인이라면, '허용되다'는 이미 정해진 규칙 안에서 가능하다는 느낌이에요. 표지판에는 '금지'의 반대로 '허용'이라고 써요.
explain_en: Used when the rules or situation don't forbid something. Where '허가되다' implies applying and receiving approval, '허용되다' means it is possible within established rules. On signs, it is the opposite of '금지'.

examples.en: The residents joined forces and solved the problem.
The harder the times, the more we need to stand together.
It's a group that works in solidarity with students from other countries.
The small shops banded together and held an event.
We want to stand with the victims.
Thanks to joining together, our strength grew.

explain: 사람들이 같은 목표나 처지 때문에 서로 힘을 모아 함께할 때 써요. 단순히 '같이하다'보다 서로 책임을 나누는 무게가 있어요. 명사 '연대'는 '연대 의식', '연대 책임'처럼 써요.
explain_en: For people pooling strength because of a shared goal or situation. It carries more weight than plain '같이하다', since it implies shared responsibility. The noun '연대' appears in '연대 의식' (sense of solidarity) and '연대 책임' (joint responsibility).

examples.ko: 교통 규칙이 위반된 경우에는 벌금을 내요.
examples.en: If traffic rules are broken, you pay a fine.

examples.ko: 계약 조건이 위반되면 취소할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the terms are violated, it can be canceled.
I felt the promise had been broken, so I got angry.
This behavior goes against school rules.
Please check so the law isn't violated.

examples.ko: 그 광고는 규정에 위반될 수 있어요.
examples.en: That ad may violate the regulations.

explain: 법·규칙·약속이 지켜지지 않았다는 결과를 말할 때 써요. '규칙을 위반하다'는 사람이 어긴 것, '규칙이 위반되다'는 규칙 쪽에서 본 표현이에요. 쉽게 말하면 '어기다'이고, 반대말은 '지키다', '준수하다'예요.
explain_en: Describes the result when a law, rule or promise is not kept. '규칙을 위반하다' is the person breaking it; '규칙이 위반되다' looks from the rule's side. The everyday verb is '어기다', and the opposites are '지키다' and '준수하다'.

examples.en: That line is often quoted in books.
This paper has been cited in many studies.
We put quotation marks on the quoted parts.
I was surprised that my post was quoted in the news.
It's a problem if something is quoted without a source.

examples.ko: 발표 자료에 인용될 문장을 골라 보세요.
examples.en: Pick sentences to be quoted in the presentation.

explain: 다른 사람의 말이나 글, 자료가 내 글이나 발표 안에 가져와 쓰일 때 써요. 내가 가져다 쓰는 쪽은 '인용하다'예요. 보고서에서는 출처를 꼭 밝혀야 하고, 말로 옮길 때는 '그 사람이 이렇게 말했어요'처럼 쉽게 말해요.
explain_en: When someone else's words, writing or data are brought into another text or talk. The person who borrows it uses '인용하다'. Reports must name the source; in speech people simply say 'he said this'.

en: close; wrap up; finish by a deadline

examples.en: We close the shop early today.
I have to finish the manuscript by Friday.
Apply before registration closes.

examples.ko: 저녁 여섯 시에 은행이 업무를 마감했어요.
examples.en: The bank closed for business at six in the evening.
We ended the season with good results this year.
After it's closed, you can't edit it.

explain: 정해진 시간이나 기한이 되어 일을 끝내고 문을 닫는 걸 말해요. 명사 '마감'은 '마감 날짜', '마감 시간'처럼 일상에서 아주 많이 써요. '끝내다'보다 기한이 정해져 있다는 느낌이 강하고, '마감 임박'은 곧 끝난다는 광고 문구예요.
explain_en: Wrapping up work and closing at a set time or deadline. The noun '마감' is very common: '마감 날짜', '마감 시간'. It stresses a fixed deadline more than '끝내다' does, and '마감 임박' is an ad phrase meaning 'closing soon'.

examples.en: Old relics had been buried underground.

examples.ko: 그 지역에는 석유가 많이 매장돼 있어요.
examples.en: There are large oil reserves in that region.
An ancient city was buried under volcanic ash.
I watched a movie about finding buried treasure.
They're surveying the places where resources lie underground.
The documents were found before being buried.

explain: 땅속에 묻혀 있을 때 써요. 유물·자원·보물처럼 파내야 찾을 수 있는 것에 많이 써요. 가게 뜻의 '매장(賣場)'과는 소리만 같고 완전히 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: For things lying underground: relics, resources, treasure that must be dug up. It only sounds like '매장' meaning 'store' (賣場); the two are different words.

examples.en: We buried our pet dog on the hill behind the house.
There are places that bury garbage in the ground.
In the old days, kings were buried in the mountains.
You have to bury it deep so it doesn't smell.
I want to bury the secret forever.
They kept records even when burying relics.

explain: 땅속에 묻을 때 써요. 장례에서 시신을 땅에 묻는 것을 말하기도 하는데, 대화에서는 '묻다'가 훨씬 쉽고 흔해요. '화장하다'(태우다)와 반대되는 방식이에요. '사회에서 매장되다'처럼 완전히 밀려나는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: Burying something in the ground, including burying a body at a funeral, although in conversation '묻다' is far easier and more common. The contrast is '화장하다' (cremate). It is also used figuratively for being shut out for good, as in '사회에서 매장되다'.

en: be controlled; be kept in check

examples.en: The temperature is controlled automatically.
The fire wasn't brought under control and spread.
This machine is run by a computer.
When emotions are kept in check, your speech softens.
You must run at a well-controlled speed.
I'm worried about whether the damage can be kept in check.

explain: 기계·온도·감정·상황이 정해진 범위 안에서 조절될 때 써요. 뉴스와 설명서에서 자주 나오고, 사람 사이에서 '통제하다'가 더 강한 느낌이에요. 컴퓨터 쪽에서는 '제어'가 기본 단어라서 '제어판', '원격 제어'처럼 많이 보여요.
explain_en: For machines, temperature, emotions or situations being kept within a set range. Frequent in news and manuals; '통제하다' feels stronger between people. In computing '제어' is the standard word, as in '제어판' (control panel) and '원격 제어'.

examples.ko: 화가 날 때는 감정을 제어하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to control your emotions when you're angry.
I control the lights at home with my smartphone.
The driver couldn't control the speed.
I'm making a program that controls a robot.

examples.ko: 식욕을 제어할 수 있는 방법이 있을까요?
examples.en: Is there a way to keep your appetite in check?
After getting the flames under control, they checked for safety.

explain: '조절하다'와 '다스리다'의 중간 느낌으로, 움직임이나 상태를 원하는 대로 다룰 때 써요. 기계나 시스템뿐 아니라 감정·욕구에도 쓰고, 사람을 억지로 누르는 건 '통제하다'가 맞아요. 멀리서 기계를 움직이는 건 '원격 제어'라고 해요.
explain_en: Between '조절하다' (adjust) and '다스리다' (govern): handling movement or condition as you want. It applies to machines and systems as well as emotions and urges. Forcing people down is '통제하다'. Operating a machine from a distance is '원격 제어'.

en: unfold; develop (of events or a story)

examples.en: The story unfolds differently from what I expected.
The drama moves fast, so it isn't boring.
I don't know how things will unfold from here.

examples.ko: 사건이 급하게 전개돼서 정리할 시간이 없었어요.
examples.en: The events moved so quickly that there was no time to sort them out.
The second half of the movie unfolded too slowly.
A new phase is unfolding.

explain: 이야기·사건·상황이 시간에 따라 펼쳐지고 이어질 때 써요. 영화·드라마 평에서 '전개가 빠르다/느리다'라고 많이 말해요. '진행되다'는 일이 이어져 가는 것, '전개되다'는 모양이 점점 드러나며 펼쳐지는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: For a story, incident or situation unfolding over time. In reviews of movies and dramas, people say '전개가 빠르다/느리다' (the plot moves fast/slow). '진행되다' is simply proceeding, while '전개되다' has the sense of a shape gradually being revealed.
